| [QUESTION-077](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-077.md) | Is agreement among an agent's interests produced by coupling, as when each sees and follows the current majority, a different kind of integration from agreement because their valuations coincide? | Drawn by the assistant from [CASE-074](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-074.md) and filed at the owner's request. | [QUESTION-131](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-131.md) | How does structural frustration among jointly incompatible demands relate to operative thwarting of a constituent's demands, and under what conditions can one occur without the other? | Raised in the reviews the owner relayed on 2026-10-18, after the filing of the exchange of 2026-10-17. Structural frustration has a settled formal definition: a collection of demands is structurally frustrated when no outcome attainable under the specified constraints meets them all, S ∉ 𝒦(𝒪; D) ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)). What is open is how it relates to operative thwarting, where a particular constituent's live demand is counteracted by an identifiable constraint or countervailing process. Physics frustration ([CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md)) is the structural sense, and self-determination theory's need thwarting ([THEORY-052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md)) the operative one. An answer says when structural incompatibility shows up as thwarting, whether thwarting can occur where joint satisfaction is possible, and what evidence attributes either to a bearer. Merely failing to realize an attainable set of requirements is neither. | Open |
